messages:
Tyler: FYI customer 'Northstar' wants a committed Dedicated pool instead of our current burst posture. They quoted 3 regions, but EU-West is the priority for Q3.
Sree: Do we have their steady-state throughput numbers? committed GPUs should map to tokens/sec or effective p50 latency SLO.
Tyler: They sent a spreadsheet — peak 1800 reqs/min for chat endpoints, avg 420 tokens per request. ops math says ~50k tokens/sec sustained. They want p50 < 150ms.
Maria: 50k tokens/sec at p50 150ms => continuous GPU load. Rough ballpark: ~30 A100-equivalent GPUs if we assume batching + kv cache. But depends on model (gpt-small vs gpt-medium quantization).
Jon: Region constraints: eu-west has limited spot capacity for 8xA100 nodes next quarter. If we commit fully there we might need to reserve host capacity from cloud provider or offer a multi-region split.
Leah: Cost check: committed 30 GPUs vs burstable 30 with 24 committed + 6 burstable — what's customer preference on cost predictability vs peak headroom?
Tyler: They want predictable invoices. They'll pay higher commit if it guarantees throughput. They're sensitive to 20% overage credits.
Sree: Suggest a phased commit: start with 18 committed in eu-west, 6 committed in us-west for failover, plus burst policy that can add +12 GPUs within 5 mins for spikes. Monitor 2 weeks, then scale to full commit if metrics stable.
Maria: +1 phased. Also propose quantized model variant for lower-cost pool (8-bit) to move lower-SLA requests. That lowers required GPUs by ~25% for some workload classes.
Jon: From infra ops side: need to validate network egress and inter-AZ bandwidth on eu-west nodes. Heavy KV cache traffic across nodes can saturate 10Gb NICs. Might push to 25Gb for safety.
Leah: On billing — BillingBot, can we surface expected monthly commit invoice for 24 vs 30 GPUs in eu-west (on-demand vs committed discounts)?
BillingBot: Estimating... 24 x A100-equivalent committed = $X/month (discounted). 30 committed = $Y/month. Burst-only baseline (no commit) = $Z/month (higher unit cost). See internal billing calc: https://redwood.internal/billing/scratch/northstar-commit.
Tyler: Also flagged: their contract requires SLA: 99.9% avail and <200ms p50. We must design fallback routing to a cheaper region if eu-west capacity harmed.
Sree: Routing policy idea: primary eu-west committed pool, fallback to us-west dedicated (lower capacity) with autoscaling limit and reduced QoS (shorter context, lower batch sizes). Implement graceful degrade: prefer cached prefixes and shorter generation lengths in fallback.
Maria: Quick sizing calc I used:
```
steady tokens/sec = (1800 req/min * 420 tokens) / 60 = 12,600 tokens/sec
add 3x headroom for peaks and batching inefficiency => ~37,800 tokens/sec
assume 1 A100-equivalent handles ~1,200 tokens/sec (with optimizations) => ~32 GPUs
```
That's why I suggested 30ish. If we can force more batching or use quantized variant, we can drop that to ~24.
Jon: For procurement: if customer signs 12-month commit we can lock discounted instance allocation with cloud partner. Need legal to add capacity protection clause.
Leah: Actionables: 1) Ops: run synthetic load test against eu-west staging with quantized and baseline models (Sree + Maria). 2) Billing: provide month-by-month commit invoice scenarios (Leah). 3) Sales/Customer: propose phased commit + 2-week canary with rollback terms (Tyler).
Sree: I'll schedule the load tests tomorrow 09:00 UTC. Can one of you share the exact model docker tags and tokenization params?
Maria: Pushed tags: redwood/gpt-chat:stable-2026-03 and redwood/gpt-chat:quant-8bit-2026-03. Tokenization config at /configs/northstar-tokenizer.yaml on the staging repo.
ops-bot: Scheduled synthetic-load test job northstar-phase1 at 2026-03-19T09:00:00Z. job-id: j-7a9f6.
Tyler: Great. I'll draft the customer proposal with phased numbers: baseline commit 18 GPUs (eu-west) + 6 GPUs (us-west), optional top-up to 12 burst GPUs. Include rollback clause and 30-day evaluation window.
Leah: Also check egress/cross-AZ premium in eu-west — that can be a sneaky 10-15% add-on to monthly cost.
BillingBot: Noted. Adding cross-AZ egress estimate for eu-west to the invoice scenarios.
Jon: One more ops note: if we pin to dedicated host groups, reduce live migration risk during maintenance windows. Need to check provider SLAs.
Tyler: Ok. Runbooks: add a pre-commit checklist: capacity check, network perf test, load test pass, SLA escalation contact, and billing acceptance confirmation. I'll open a doc and link it here when ready.
Sree: Will post load test results + perf graphs in this thread after run completes.
Maria: If perf is within 10% of predicted, we can move to contract negotiation. If it's worse, we'll propose larger quantized fraction.
Tyler: Thanks all. Leaning to phased commit recommendation. I'll follow up with draft proposal by EOD.
